newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen weighed on by auction.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen weighed on by auction.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds could underperform Bunds ahead of new supply on Monday but the underlying tone was still firm, dealers said on Thursday.

"Each time the spread (over Bunds) gets to near 10 basis points we see buyers both from abroad and here," one said. "People look at France and see it trading 15 basis points under and say why can't Belgium be flat."

The spread of the benchmark March 2007 OLO over Bunds widened slightly on Friday to nine basis points from seven as buyers stayed away for most of the session after U.S. Treasuries sold off on Wednesday in a surprise reaction to inflation data.

One trader noted many players took advantage of favourable prices at Tuesday's exchange auction to swap from short-dated paper into the benchmark, expecting the market to rise, and were caught when the market turned lower. "When there's an overhang there is no selling, but because there were no buyers either Belgium was pushed a bit wider."
Higher-than-expected German money supply data and a rise in German business sentiment also dented the start of trade.
But prices in the benchmark squeezed back up higher in late dealings, with the yield edging back down toward its Wednesday close of 5.60 percent.
"I expect it to strengthen further if the currency firms more," one trader said.

The Belgian franc, which has been under pressure due to a raft of scandals in a governing political party, ended the day off its lows at 20.6365/95 to the mark, up from 20.6410/30 at Wednesday's close.
